title: Intersection commutes with nonempty small directed unions of subobjects
statement: Let u, v, w be universe levels, C : Type u a category with homs in Type v, and assume [Abelian C] and [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C] [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. For X : C, a nonempty index type ι : Type w, a subobject S of X, and T : ι → Subobject X with Directed (· ≤ ·) T, one has S ⊓ (⨆ i, T i) = ⨆ i, S ⊓ T i. The index universe w is the same universe as the Grothendieck-abelian instance; no equality of u, v, and w is assumed.

source.place: Line 53, CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.inf_iSup_of_directed; universe and section hypotheses at lines 32-47; AB5 context: Stacks Tag 079A.

proof.text: Put the preorder induced by T on ι. Directedness and nonemptiness make it filtered. The monotone families T i and S ⊓ T i define diagrams of monomorphisms over X. Their suprema are colimits of the underlying diagrams in C, by the Grothendieck-abelian subobject-colimit theorem.

For each i, the sequence S ⊓ T i → T i → cokernel(S.arrow) is exact: the first map is the kernel of the second. Assemble these sequences into a short complex of functors on ι. Exactness of filtered colimits and connectedness of ι give the exact sequence (⨆ i, S ⊓ T i) → (⨆ i, T i) → cokernel(S.arrow).

The kernel universal property factors the inclusion of S ⊓ (⨆ i, T i) through ⨆ i, S ⊓ T i, proving the forward inequality. Each S ⊓ T i is bounded by both S and ⨆ i, T i, so their supremum gives the reverse inequality.
